messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
Below is a concise but comprehensive snapshot of key Texas traffic laws as of 2025‑2026 (the most recent statutes and administrative rules). If you’re looking for something more detailed—e.g., how penalties vary by county, or how new “smart” road signs affect enforcement—just let me know! --- ### 1️⃣ General Roadway Rules | Topic | What it means | Typical Penalties | |-------|---------------|-------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• In residential areas, default limit is 35 mph if no sign posted.
• School zones: 25 mph during school hours (or 20 mph when children present). | Fine $100–$500 + points; higher fines & possible license suspension for repeated violations. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop before entering intersections where another vehicle has priority.
• At four‑way stops, first‑come, first‑served rule applies. | Points added to driver’s record; repeat offenders may face license suspensions. | | **Headlights/Signal Use** | • Headlamps required from sunset to sunrise, after dark, or in fog/rain.
• Turn signals mandatory 30 ft before turning or changing lanes. | Fines up to $200; points. | --- ### 2️⃣ Seat Belt & Child Safety Laws | Category | Requirement | Enforcement Notes | |----------|-------------|--------------------| | **Seat Belts** | All occupants must wear belts. Front seats require lap+shoulder harnesses; rear seats only lap belts allowed. | Failure → fine $50–$150 plus one point. | | **Child Restraint Systems** | Children under 8 years *must* use approved child safety restraints appropriate for their size/weight. | Violations carry a $75–$250 fine and a point. | | **Bicycle Helmets** | Riders <18 must wear helmets. | Fine $10–$40 per violation. | --- ### 3️⃣ Alcohol & Drug‑Related Driving | Law | Key Provisions | Penalty Range | |-----|-----------------|--------------| | **DUI / DWI** | Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥0.08% = DUI. Lower BAC thresholds exist for commercial drivers and those under 21. | First offense: $300–$600 fine, 90 days jail, 12‑month license revocation. Repeat offenses increase fines, longer jail terms, and extended license suspensions. | | **Impaired Vehicle Operation (IVI)** | Operating a motor vehicle while impaired by drugs (including prescription meds) without medical clearance. | Similar to DUI penalties; additional drug‑specific charges may apply. | | **Open Container** | Any open container of alcoholic beverage inside passenger area prohibited. | Fine $125–$350. | --- ### 4️⃣ Distracted Driving Regulations | Rule | Details | Consequences | |------|---------|--------------| | **Texting While Driving** | Disallowed for all drivers regardless of age. Includes sending, reading, replying, or typing text messages. | Fine $100–$400; points. | | **Phone Calls** | Allowed only via hands‑free devices. Using handheld phone while driving is illegal. | Same penalty range as texting. | | **Other Distractions** | Eating, applying makeup, using GPS apps, playing music loudly, etc., considered distractions if they impair safe operation. | Minor infractions usually result in warning; serious cases treated as reckless driving. | --- ### 5️⃣ Commercial Driver Specifics | Issue | Statute | Penalty Highlights | |-------|--------|--------------------| | **Commercial Driver's License (CDL) Hours of Service** | Must adhere to federal HOS regs; state adds extra restrictions for hazardous materials. | Violation leads to CDL demerit points, potential suspension, and civil liability. | | **Drug Testing** | Mandatory random testing for Class A/B truckers. | Non‑compliance results in immediate suspension until test completed. | | **Vehicle Inspection** | Annual inspection required for heavy trucks. | Failure to comply can lead to impoundment and fines. | --- ### 6️⃣ Parking & Traffic Control | Regulation | Summary | Common Offenses | |------------|---------|------------------| | **Parking Restrictions** | No parking within 15 ft of stop lines, fire hydrants, or pedestrian crossings. | Ticketed ($60–$120); towing fees add cost. | | **Traffic Signals** | Red light running, green‑light running, and failure to yield at roundabouts are prosecuted. | Fines $200–$800; points; possible license suspension. | | **School Bus Stops** | Vehicles must stop behind red lights and wait until bus resumes motion. | Heavy fines ($500+) and points. | --- ### 7️⃣ Emerging Tech & Smart Infrastructure | Technology | How It Works | Legal Implications | |-----------|--------------|--------------------| | **Smart Speed Cameras** | Automated cameras detect speeding and issue tickets electronically. | Tickets mailed directly to registered owner; no court appearance needed. | | **Connected Car Alerts** | Some counties now send real‑time alerts for accidents or congestion. | Drivers expected to heed warnings; ignoring them could be deemed negligent. | | **Electronic Toll Collection** | TxTag system automatically deducts tolls; non‑payment triggers automated notices. | Late payments accrue interest; persistent delinquency can lead to account closure. | --- ### 8️⃣ Resources & Where to Find More Info | Resource | Access | Why It Helps | |----------|--------|--------------| | **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – [txdot.gov](https://www.txdot.gov/) | Official site | Latest updates on roadway projects, signage changes, and public service announcements. | | **Texas Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC)** – [mvc.texas.gov](http://www.mvc.state.tx.us/) | Licensing portal | Detailed DMV forms, fee schedules, and licensing requirements. | | **TexCode Online** – [law.justia.com/codes/texas/traffic-laws] | Full statutory code | Read the exact legal wording for each statute. | | **Local County Courts’ Websites** | Court docket access | View case outcomes, sentencing trends, and local ordinances. | | **Legal Aid Organizations** – e.g., Texas RioGrande Legal Aid | Free counsel | Assistance if facing traffic citations or criminal charges. | --- #### Quick Tips for Staying Compliant 1. **Always keep your driver's handbook handy** – it contains updated tables for speed limits, seat‑belt mandates, and other nuances. 2. **Use a hands‑free device** whenever you need to talk on the phone. 3. **Check your mileage log** if you drive commercially; missing entries can trigger penalties. 4. **Stay informed about temporary construction detours** – many are posted online weeks ahead. 5. **Keep receipts for toll tags** and pay promptly to avoid late‑fee surcharges. Feel free to dive deeper into any section—or request examples of typical ticket scenarios!
message.reasoning:
The user wants information on traffic laws in Texas. We can provide an overview or specific aspects like speed limits, seat belt law, DUI regulations, texting while driving, etc.

We might also ask clarifying question? But likely they want general info. Provide summary and maybe references. No need to call function because it's not searching lawsuits; just providing knowledge. So answer with details.
